identity.name: ALLCARGO TERMINALS LTD
identity.industry: Logistics / Container Freight Stations & ICD Infrastructure

summary.oneLiner: Allcargo Terminals is accelerating its 3-year plan to handle 1 million TEUs by expanding capacity at JNPT and Mundra, with regulatory approvals secured and capex funded via equity infusion and internal cash flow, driving industry-leading EBITDA per TEU of INR 2,292 and margin resilience despite flat revenue.

one-line thesis: Allcargo Terminals is accelerating its 3-year plan to handle 1 million TEUs by expanding capacity at JNPT and Mundra, with regulatory approvals secured and capex funded via equity infusion and internal cash flow, driving industry-leading EBITDA per TEU of INR 2,292 and margin resilience despite flat revenue.
financial scorecard: revenue: -1.6% YoY (INR187cr vs INR190cr); EBITDA: +16.7% YoY (INR35cr vs INR30cr); EBITDA margin: +400 bps YoY to 18.7%; PAT: -10% YoY (INR9cr vs INR10cr) due to one-off tax adjustment in Q1FY25; order book: N/A (no order book in CFS business); net debt: INR100cr (planned repayment via internal accruals)
guidance: revenue growth: 6-6.5% aligned with India EXIM trade; margin: sustain EBITDA/TEU at INR2,000+; order inflow: no explicit guidance; capex/commissioning: INR450-500cr over 3 years, with Mundra Phase 1 (INR75cr) and Farukhnagar ICD (INR215cr) as key projects
segment / subsidiary detail: JNPT: +25 acres capacity added in Q1; Mundra: renewed CWC concession + 60-acre land acquisition for new CFS; Farukhnagar: IMC approval received for greenfield ICD; Chennai: capacity expansion under evaluation; Dadri: operational with CONCOR rail partnership; total current capacity: 8.3 lakh TEUs; target: 13 lakh TEUs by FY28
growth verticals / optionality: Vadhavan Port (3-4 years away); potential Chennai expansion; digital myCFS portal integration with customs systems; Allcargo Group synergies (ocean freight, warehousing) driving captive volume
margins & cost dynamics: EBITDA/TEU: INR2,292 in Q1FY26 (+22% YoY); gross margin improved to 36% from 32% YoY; opex efficiency driven by scale in transport/equipment contracts and digital automation; Mundra Phase 1 will reduce rental costs; JNPT expansion will share fixed costs across higher volume
capex / expansion: INR450-500cr over 3 years; already spent INR110cr on HORCL rail at Farukhnagar; Mundra Phase 1: INR75cr (to add 1 lakh TEU capacity); Farukhnagar ICD: INR215cr; total capex funded by internal accruals (strong DSO of 18-20 days), INR38cr equity infusion via warrants, and minimal bridge debt (INR50-70cr)
capital allocation: Priority: fund capex (70%) via internal cash flow + equity infusion; secondary: repay INR100cr debt to reduce interest cost; no dividends or buybacks mentioned; no external debt dependency planned
risks & watch-items: tariff uncertainty (U.S. impact deemed minimal on CFS cargo mix); delayed DFC implementation; port-led competition (e.g., Adani EXIM yard in Mundra); regulatory delays in Chennai expansion; inflationary capex cost escalation
management quality / tone: highly confident and execution-focused; emphasized milestone achievements (approvals secured), discipline on profitability (EBITDA/TEU), and capital efficiency; tone optimistic on India trade growth and ATL’s differentiated position
non-obvious takeaways: Allcargo Terminals benefits from captive volume via Allcargo Group’s integrated logistics chain (ocean freight, warehousing), providing stable demand unlike pure-play CFS peers; digital myCFS portal is first-of-its-kind in industry, creating customer lock-in and operational efficiency

themes.title: Logistics, ports & supply-chain formalization
themes.need: E-commerce, quick-commerce and GST-driven warehousing consolidation plus a 1P->3P shift drive an integrated-logistics up-cycle. DELHIVERY hit early FCF (>1B parcels, Express +46% rev) with Express targeting 16-18% margin; CONCOR/GATEWAY/JSWINFRA on rail/ports; ALLCARGO/MAHLOG/TVSSCS/VRLLOG on 3PL/road; BLUEDART/TCIEXP/WCIL/SNOWMAN on express + cold-chain; DELHIVERY/SHADOWFAX on quick-commerce fulfilment. Q1FY27's clearest turnaround datapoint: MAHLOG swung to a +INR 25.4cr PAT from a -INR 10.8cr loss on +23% revenue, with B2B Express (Rivigo) gross margin turning +6% from -3.8% and its EBITDA loss cut to -INR 1.6cr from -INR 11.8cr, guided to EBITDA breakeven within FY27, while Contract Logistics grew 26% with margin diluted only ~46bps on new-site start-up costs (opening a site almost every week).
themes.driver: Express/quick-commerce volume momentum; warehousing leasing; port/rail throughput; operating-leverage inflection.
